identification: Lot 1106, title SLAB OF SASSAFRAS. The one photo shows three rough-sawn live-edge slabs standing against a shed wall, about 2 m long; the lot is the middle slab (chalk reads 106x/20/11/26). The wood is pale, spalted with dark speckling and some knots, not the dark heart typical of blackheart. Unseasoned, natural edge, checks at ends. Gowans sells these in a continuous series, so supply is regular and prices are low.

viewing_check: Measure length, width and thickness (a slab over 5 cm thick and 40 cm wide is worth more); check for dark blackheart streaking on the cut ends, splits or end checks running into the body, insect damage, and whether it is air-dried or green. Photograph the end grain and both faces.
